title: Choose the ClearCam layout
question: All three retain the approved household-observatory world. Pick the structure that should guide the redesigned local Mac dashboard, or tell me what to combine.

options.label: Live view + tonight’s log
options.lineage: one observation window and a concise notebook margin
options.thesis: The active camera is the present; the side log explains what mattered.
options.viewport: A dominant live view takes the left; tonight’s event log and camera setup action sit in a narrow right rail.
options.risk: The timeline needs a strong empty state when there are no events.

options.label: Camera reel + daily journal
options.lineage: a contact strip above a carefully ordered daybook
options.thesis: Choose a camera in seconds, then read the day as one coherent record.
options.viewport: A horizontal camera reel opens the app; the lower surface balances a chronological event journal with a health ledger.
options.risk: A busy multi-camera home could make the top reel feel visually dense.

options.label: Observations timeline
options.lineage: a day’s field observations arranged along a single clear track
options.thesis: The event record is the product; cameras and health are supporting instruments.
options.viewport: A camera selector stays left, a rich vertical event timeline fills the center, and a narrow inspector shows the current system state.
options.risk: It makes the live camera less immediate for owners who mainly want to check right now.
